items.title: Arthur Baron interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 3, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: this great gig I had for The Duke’s Men, I think I told you about it where I had Bill Crow, the 90 some odd year old bass player, and Bernard Purdie, the great drummer.

ctx.x: Well the last gig, this great gig I had for The Duke’s Men, I think I told you about it where I had Bill Crow, the 90 some odd year old bass player, and Bernard Purdie, the great drummer. By the way Purdie swings his butt off. You know I remember meeting him in Richmond, Virginia at a jazz party, oh gosh, probably 30 years ago maybe. And you know these big parties with a whole group of musicians and they put you together. And my first band I played with he was playing drums and I was like oh my God. I told him,…

send one of their agents over. All this was about to happen, and I was like this feels like a resurrection. It feels right. It feels like something to put my time in. And I have this friend of mine named Monk Rowe who got me a gig on October 30, which still are like this. Because I just talked to Purdie last night and I told him about it. Because I wanted to wait just a little more. But good news is better to give than bad news. So so far it’s good news man, and we greatly appreciate that.
